title: Land and Sea Use Planning
description: By 2040, at least 24% of terrestrial and inland water, and 16% of marine and coastal areas accomplished biodiversity inclusive spatial analysis and planning
actions: Actions necessary to achieve the national target: Formulation and adoption of management Plans for Protected Areas and OECMs with geo-spatial plans on land use, vulnerability and risks, tenurial instruments Geo-spatial Plans: Develop geo-spatial plans that overlay land use, vulnerability, risks, and tenurial instruments. Relevant stakeholders include DENR, specifically the Land Management Bureau (LMB), in collaboration with LGUs, NEDA, and other relevant government agencies. Conduct of Management Effectiveness Assessment using the Management Effectiveness Tracking Tool (METT) or MEAT in Protected Areas and OECMs Development of a policy that will install ARA compliance Integration of Spatial Planning within Protected Areas (PAs) Management Plans: Ensure that all protected areas under the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS/eNIPAS) and Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECM) Registry have integrated spatial planning in their conservation and management plans. Relevant stakeholders include the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), specifically the Biodiversity Management Bureau (BMB), in collaboration with the Protected Area Management Boards (PAMBs), LGUs, NCIP and the Indigenous People (for the ICCAs), other relevant stakeholders for the OECMs. Expansion of OECM Registry Participation: Increase the participation of the different government agencies, LGUs, private sector, civil society, academia, and other sectors in the OECM Registry. Relevant stakeholders include the DENR-BMB, in coordination with various government agencies, LGUs, and stakeholders. Inclusive Planning Process: Ensure the participation of women and men, including Indigenous Peoples (IP) and non-IP communities, in the planning process, maintaining at least a 60-40 ratio. Relevant stakeholders include DENR-BMB, National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), and LGUs. Allocate funds to implement the approved management plans. These actions, when implemented in coordination and collaboration with national government agencies and other stakeholders, will enable the Philippines to achieve its target of effectively planning and managing all areas to reduce biodiversity loss by 2040.

title: Ecosystem Restoration
description: By 2040, at least 30% of degraded terrestrial (upland and lowland), inland water, coastal, and marine ecosystems restored/rehabilitated, resulting to enhanced biodiversity, ecosystem functions, ecological integrity, and connectivity
actions: To achieve the target of restoring 30% of all degraded ecosystems by 2040 in the Philippines, the following actions have been identified: Identification of Degraded Areas: Conduct dialogues to achieve a shared understanding of biologically degraded areas and agree on action steps for restoration. Conduct comprehensive assessments to identify ecologically and biologically degraded terrestrial, inland water, coastal, and marine ecosystems. The relevant stakeholders include the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA), scientific institutions, local government units (LGUs), indigenous communities. These would require environmental assessments, biodiversity surveys, and remote sensing data among others. Development of Restoration/Rehabilitation Plans: Detailed restoration and rehabilitation plans for selected degraded sites should be prepared, incorporating scientific assessments, community input, and stakeholder consultations. The relevant stakeholders include the DENR, LGUs, Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Science and Technology (DOST), academic institutions, NGOs, indigenous communities. Critical information from the academe (ecosystem restoration methodologies and guidelines), some scientific research and stakeholder (community consultations) is needed. Restoration or rehabilitation plans would include NAPERSEP, NGP, Implementation of Restoration Activities: The execution of the approved restoration plans (i.e. reforestation, habitat restoration, soil conservation, waterway rehabilitation, and marine ecosystem restoration) will follow with the collaboration of relevant stakeholders like the DENR, LGUs, DA, Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG), private sector partners, NGOs, communities. At this point implementation guidelines, project management plans, and standardized monitoring protocols are essential. Capacity Building and Training: Training and capacity-building programs to equip stakeholders with the necessary skills and knowledge for effective ecosystem restoration and management should be given. Important stakeholders include the DENR, LGUs, academic institutions, NGOs, indigenous communities, and the local community. The need for the development of training modules and the conduct of workshops would ensue (Target 20). Monitoring and Evaluation: Similar to the other targets with actions or indicators identified

title: Protect and Conserve Land and Sea
description: By 2040, at least 24% of terrestrial and inland water, and 16% of coastal and marine areas are effectively conserved and managed (especially areas of particular importance for biodiversity and ecosystem functions and services).
actions: The main document here would be the OECM list being drafted by the DENR which would consolidate in the list the different areas being protected by different agencies and people. This includes: LGU – protected areas; KBAs, reference ecosystems of the mining areas, biodiversity corridors wherein priority species move or inhabit. The ancestral domains of the IPs although part of the protected area (protection by the IPs) may not be included in the OECM but will be included in the tabulation of the protected areas. There are more areas which have been identified but these are being validated and some need to undergo stakeholders consultation or agreements. To support the achievement of the target to conserve 30% of land and sea by 2040 in the Philippines, several actions involving various stakeholders should be taken. Identification and Designation of New Protected Areas: Identification of potential OECMs, numerical targets for 30x30, keystone/threatened species Involvement of government agencies/ LGUs/ private sector/ civil society/ academe/ other sectors on the establishment/designation/management of OECMs and updating the OECM Registry Designate new protected areas under the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act and Expanded NIPAS Act. Conduct comprehensive assessments to identify ecologically significant areas deserving protection (these would include locally managed MPAs, KBAs, ICCAs, and OECMs). Engage with indigenous peoples and local communities to recognize and integrate their territories into protected area management plans (ancestral domains). The ancestral domains are large tracts of land and marine areas (ancestral domain waters) which could be a huge contribution to the 30% target. Tabulate the areas of protection under several levels of protection to ensure the 30% protection of land and sea. Development of Ecologically Sound and Inclusive Conservation and Management Plans: Formulation and adoption of management Plans for Protected Areas and OECMs with geo-spatial plans on land use, vulnerability and risks, tenurial instruments Adoption of Management Plans for Protected Areas and OECMs with Geo-spatial plans on land use, vulnerability and risks, tenurial instruments Allocate adequate funding for the implementation of these plans, including resources for biodiversity monitoring, enforcement, and community engagement. Establishment of Functioning Management Bodies: Assess the status of each governance body viz target sites Develop

title: Active Management of Species and Genetic Diversity
description: By 2040, governance and management regimes are improved for threatened species; native crops, livestocks, wild relatives; and their genetic resources
actions: Actions which will be taken to achieve the national target includes: Assessment and Monitoring of Threatened Species (for different taxa) included in the national list using the Red List Index (agreed upon by experts). The assessment of the species should be a continuing activity for both terrestrial (with freshwater) and marine species. This includes the creation of maps: to include distribution and routes (of migratory species) to establish locations. These will facilitate local participation in conservation and monitoring. Establishment of native species seed banks and nurseries to conserve genetic diversity and ensure the availability of native plant species for restoration and conservation efforts in several areas in the country. This is linked to the restoration of degraded habitats as per Target 2. Development and Implementation of Conservation Plans for priority threatened wildlife species. This includes habitat protection, population management, and local stakeholder engagement (most specially for continuous species monitoring). Linked to Targets 1, 2 and 3. Improvement of Wild Populations of Economically Important Species via habitat restoration (Target 2), sustainable harvesting practices (Target 5), and fisheries management (Target 3, 5). Establishment and Maintenance of Wildlife Rescue Centers both terrestrial and aquatic/marine wildlife rescue centers to provide care, rehabilitation, and release of injured or displaced wildlife. Conservation of Migratory Species and Wetlands by protecting routes of migratory species in inland and coastal wetlands sites through the establishment of a network of protected areas or biodiversity corridors, habitat restoration, and community-based conservation initiatives (Targets 2 and 3). Protection of native livestock by continuing and supporting efforts of academe and other research agencies instituting genetic conservation programs, sustainable breeding practices. Another would be supporting traditional livestock farming communities (e.g. IPs – Target 22). These actions would contribute to the achievement of other specific targets of the KMGBF and the PBSAP. Relevant agencies are DENR, DA and NGOs.

title: Harvest, Trade, and Use of Wild Species
description: By 2040, wildlife species harvested from the wild are traded within the allowed limits and conditions set by RA 9147 (Wildlife Act), By 2030, the Harvest Control Rules and Reference Points for capture fisheries under RA 10654 and its IRR are in place
actions: Several policy measures and actions will be done to achieve the Philippine target: Fortified with full time staff, budget and authority, the National Convergence Initiative (NCI) which will ensure harmonization and mainstreaming biodiversity in all relevant priority programs and projects that utilize/ impact on natural resources/ecosystems should be fully implemented. (NEDA) Development of science-based allowable harvest limits and harvesting guidelines for priority species in terrestrial, coastal, and marine ecosystems, established in accordance with the provisions set forth in Republic Act No. 9147 (Wildlife Act) and its implementing rules and regulations (Joint DENR-DA-PCSD AO 2004-01). Addition of economic incentives and policies to encourage stakeholders to shift towards less destructive means of harvesting wild species. This may include tax incentives, subsidies, and market-based mechanisms to promote sustainable harvesting practices (Target 18). Implement measures to reduce by-catch of vulnerable and target species through the use of selective fishing gear and practices. This would include the strengthened efforts to combat illegal trade of wildlife through increased monitoring, surveillance, and law enforcement activities. Strengthen wildlife regulation and enforcement activities by enhancing coordination among agencies, increasing patrols and inspections, and increasing penalties for wildlife-related offenses (Target 3, NCI). Capacitate an appropriate number of enforcers to perform their duties effectively in regulating wildlife trade which includes training, providing equipment, and support to enforcement personnel (Target 3, 4, 20). Implement components of the Zoonoses program, including the Philippine Surveillance System, to monitor and address zoonotic diseases transmitted from wildlife to humans. Adopt and implement the One Health program to promote interdisciplinary collaboration and holistic approaches to health management, including planetary health considerations. Issue seed collection guidelines for native and endemic species to ensure sustainable harvesting practices. Baseline inventories of native Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) to assess their status and inform sustainable management strategies will be conducted. Develop audience-specific (harvesters, traders, buyers) educational materials and require them to undertake sustained CEPA on comprehensive issues emanating from illegal use/trade (Target 20)

title: Invasive Alien Species
description: By 2040, the spread of invasive alien species (IAS) reduced by 50% in priority sites.
actions: The NISSAP was crafted and adopted jointly by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR and the Department of Agriculture (DA) (Joint DENR-DA AO 2020-02) in pursuit of the objectives of: the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act (Republic Act No. 9147), the Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act (Republic Act No. 11038), the Plant Quarantine Law (Presidential Decree No. 1433), the Amended Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 (Republic Act No. 10654), and the Philippine commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), and to address the threats of invasive alien species (IAS) to Philippine biodiversity, economy and social welfare. These are taken from the joint administrative order: There are nine (9) strategic goals towards a holistic, collaborative and multi-sectoral approach in managing the risks of IAS: (1) leadership and coordination; (2) prevention; (3) early detection and rapid response; (4) control and management; (5) restoration; (6) research and information management; (7) education and public awareness; (8) international cooperation; and (9) training needs. Each of the nine strategic goals provide its guiding principles, objectives, implementing guidelines and planned actions spanning three timelines - short term (2020-2021), medium term (2022-2023) and long term (2024-2030). The joint resolution stipulates that: the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) through the Biodiversity Management Bureau (BMB), Ecosystems Research and Development Bureau (ERDB), Forest Management Bureau (FMB), and Environmental Management Bureau (EMB); and the Department of Agriculture (DA) through the Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI), Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), and Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI) shall disseminate the NISSAP, undertake capacity building for field offices and other relevant agencies, coordinate the conduct of surveys and researches, undertake public awareness campaigns, and develop specific policy guidelines to ensure efficient and effective implementation of the NISSAP by all concerned. In addition, the DENR, through the BMB and the DA through its Policy Research Service shall facilitate the creation of the inter-agency coordinating body for IAS. Further, both the DENR and DA, in collaboration with other concerned agencies and stakeholders are hereby authorized to coordinate the implementation and mainstreaming of the NISSAP with the plans and programs

title: Reduce Pollution
description: By 2040, reduce nutrient run-off and pesticide-related impacts on non-target organisms and ecosystem by at least 50%
actions: Actions for this target should be under the jurisdiction of several government agencies. The DA and the DENR should have a joint resolution to collaborate and achieve the national target regarding agricultural waste. The DENR with the DILG, leagues of municipalities and cities should also have a resolution for addressing household waste. The DENR (EMB) addresses industrial waste. Invest in training programs and capacity- building initiatives for agricultural stakeholders to promote awareness and understanding of sustainable agricultural practices and pollution reduction measures (DA). Support research initiatives focused on developing and promoting biodiversity-friendly and toxic-free agricultural inputs and practices. Foster collaboration between research institutions, agricultural universities, and the private sector to innovate solutions (DA). Strengthen extension services to provide technical assistance and guidance to farmers on adopting sustainable farming methods, including organic farming, integrated pest management, and soil conservation practices (DA). Provide financial incentives, subsidies, and grants to farmers who transition to sustainable agricultural practices and invest in pollution reduction measures. Establish financing mechanisms to support the adoption of environmentally friendly technologies and inputs (Target 19) (DA). Enact and enforce regulations that promote sustainable agriculture and pollution reduction, including laws banning or restricting the use of harmful chemicals and inorganic fertilizers. Ensure compliance with environmental standards and monitor agricultural activities for pollution prevention (DA). Preparation of information on baselines of pesticide and other pollutants (classified according to types, degree and extent of impacts, users, etc.). Implementation of phased-out or reduced use programs for harmful chemical, inorganic fertilizers, pesticides and other pollutants. Monitoring of water quality from 2023 levels. Facilitate market access for producers of biodiversity-friendly and organic agricultural products by providing market information, certification support, and access to fair trade networks. Foster collaboration between government agencies, civil society organizations, academic institutions, and the private sector to coordinate efforts and share best practices in pollution reduction and sustainable agriculture.

title: Minimize the Impact of Climate Change
description: By 2040, the impacts of climate change are minimized and disaster risks reduced through Nature-based solutions and/or Ecosystem-based approaches, and relevant indigenous knowledge systems and practices
actions: To achieve Target 8, a series of strategic actions are needed. Increase the Number of Climate-proofed Protected Area Management Plans Prepare baseline information (with vulnerability assessment report) per target against threats/climate perils (historical and/or probabilistic). Conduct vulnerability and risk assessments in terrestrial, coastal, marine and other natural ecosystems Identify the most significant climate change threats to each protected area, including risks from increased temperatures, sea-level rise, extreme weather events, and ocean acidification. Mainstream Nature-based Solutions (NBS) Across Sectoral Plans Prepare NBS prescriptions in vulnerable areas. Design nature-based solutions tailored to each protected area's unique ecosystems and threats, focusing on restoring and conserving natural habitats to enhance resilience against climate change. Climate- proof and incorporate NBS prescriptions of Protected Area Management Plan, LLCAP, NCCAP/NAP, NDRMM,CLUP(CDRA), Watershed Management Plan, among others adopted and implemented (with vulnerability & risk assessments; Nature-based solutions Programs, Activities, and Projects (NBS PAPs); climate insurance, Automated Weather Station (AWS), etc) Enhance Ecosystem Resilience: Strengthen the resilience of ecosystems within protected areas through reforestation, mangrove restoration, and the protection of coral reefs to reduce the impact of storms, flooding, and other disasters. Adopt and Enforce Stricter Zoning and Land-Use Policies: Prevent development and activities that could increase vulnerability to climate impacts, such as deforestation, unsustainable tourism, and construction in high-risk areas. Increase coastline planted to mangroves Legislate/pass national policy on greenbelts Integrate NBS into National and Local Development Plans: Work with relevant government agencies to ensure that nature-based solutions are incorporated into broader national and local development, agriculture, fisheries, and urban planning policies. Promote Cross- sectoral Collaboration: Foster partnerships between government agencies, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, and local communities to implement and scale up nature-based solutions. Implement Climate risk insurance Conduct studies on the effects of climate change on the priority threatened species Secure Funding for NBS Initiatives : Identify and tap into national and international funding sources, including the Green Climate Fund, for project

title: Sustainable Use and Benefit-Sharing
description: By 2040, wildlife species harvested from the wild are traded within the allowed limits and conditions set by RA 9147 (Wildlife Act), By 2030, the Harvest Control Rules and Reference Points for capture fisheries under RA 10654 and its IRR are in place
actions: The measures and actions are not going to be achieved without the actions of various stakeholders from the NGAs (DENR, DA, DILG, NCIP, NEDA, DILG (LGUs), DOST, CHED (SUCs)) (and their line agencies), NGOs, ACB, etc. To achieve the indicators listed for KMGBF Target 9 in the Philippines, several activities need to be implemented (in collaborations with other relevant agencies/stakeholders) to provide information for each indicator. Implement actions to minimize impacts of unsustainable practices on wildlife : Strict enforcement of laws and policies against illegal trade of wildlife Conduct a review of existing wildlife protection laws and regulations to identify gaps and areas for improvement. Develop and implement new policies and regulations targeting hunting, poaching, and illegal wildlife trade, with a focus on protecting vulnerable and migratory species. Strengthen law enforcement agencies and capacity to combat wildlife crime through training, equipment provision, and collaboration with other agencies and stakeholders. Establish partnerships with international organizations and neighboring countries to address transboundary issues related to wildlife conservation and illegal trade. Issuance of wildlife permits Compliance monitoring of permit holders Determination of annual quota for wild collection (with conditions to address sustainability issues). Document by-catch of vulnerable and target species (DENR, DA: BFAR): Reporting and active monitoring of by-catch of vulnerable and target species Conduct comprehensive surveys and assessments of harvesting, hunting and fishing activities in different terrestrial, marine and freshwater ecosystems to quantify by-catch of vulnerable and target species. Monitoring of wild populations of economically important terrestrial and aquatic species Develop monitoring programs and protocols to record and document by-catch data, including species composition, quantities, and harvesting, hunting and fishing methods used. Engage gatherers, hunters and fishers and local and fishing communities in participatory monitoring and data collection efforts to enhance accuracy and coverage. Analyze by-catch data to identify trends, hotspots, and potential mitigation measures to reduce impacts on vulnerable species. Conduct ecological carrying capacity assessments: Conduct scientific studies and assessments to determine the ecological carrying capacity of marine and freshwater ecosystems, including factors such as habitat suitabilit

title: Sustainable Management of Agriculture, Aquaculture, and Forestry
description: By 2040, agriculture, fisheries, aquaculture, and forestry production levels are sustainably managed, resilience improved and long-term productivity maintained 70% upland agricultural landscapes (areas) within KBAs and watershed forest reserves implement biodiversity-friendly agricultural practices. 50% of all rice and corn areas deemed suitable for commodity systems, lowland modality of BDFAP are under that modality as defined by the NAFMIP (Note: Target for lowland and upland)
actions: Promotion and Adoption of Biodiversity-Friendly Agricultural Practices (DA-ATI, BFAR; DENR FMB): Identification of production zones in each target site and promotion of adoption of climate smart, sustainable, and biodiversity-friendly forestry, agriculture, fishery and aquatic production practices. Develop and implement training programs and extension services to educate farmers about the benefits and techniques of biodiversity-friendly practices such as organic farming, Sustainable Land Management (SLM) technologies, and Integrated Pest Management (IPM). Provide financial incentives and technical support to farmers who adopt biodiversity-friendly practices, including subsidies for organic certification and access to alternative pest management solutions. Establish demonstration farms and model villages to showcase successful implementation of biodiversity-friendly practices and their positive impacts on productivity and sustainability. Provide material, financial and technical support to willing SLM adopters especially during the transition to BDFAPs wherein expected incomes may be reduced Collaborate with agricultural cooperatives, non- governmental organizations (NGOs), and private sector partners to disseminate information and facilitate knowledge exchange among farmers. Establishing the practice of using the supply chain and value chain principles in local commerce including preparation of habitat and production plan Creation of measures of gauging the improvement in local trade and economy due to good farming and conservation practices. *consult with NEDA Expansion of Sustainable Forest Management (DENR FMB, Target 3): Conduct comprehensive assessments of forest resources to identify priority areas for sustainable forest management, focusing on increasing the coverage of production forests. Develop and implement forest management plans that integrate biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, and community livelihoods, with active involvement of local stakeholders. Strengthen law enforcement and monitoring mechanisms to prevent illegal logging, forest encroachment, and unsustainable harvesting practices. Promote community-based forest management approaches, recognizing the rights and traditional knowledge of indigenous peoples and local communities. Development of the Philippine Agrobiodiversity Index:(DA) Establish a multidisciplinary task force composed of experts from relevant government agencies, research institutions, and civil society organ

title: Regulation of Air, Hazards and Extreme Events
description: By 2040, resilience and stability of ecosystems and habitats are maintained and enhanced, especially those in vulnerable areas/situations and high exposure areas, and those communities most dependent on biodiversity.
actions: To achieve Target 11 the Philippines needs to take a series of strategic actions aligned with identified indicators. Below is a plan of action for each identified indicator: Conduct Post Disaster Needs Assessments (PDNA) in Priority Protected Areas (PAs) and Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) Conduct of Post Disaster Needs Assessments (PDNA) / blue and green assessment (BGA) in priority PAs after every disaster Develop and Implement a Standardized PDNA Protocol: Tailor this protocol for ecosystems and biodiversity, focusing on assessing the impact of disasters on the living conditions and livelihood of IPLC women and men living within PAs and OECMs and ecosystem services and biodiversity in priority PAs and OECMs. Train Teams in PDNA: Build capacity among local government units (LGUs), environmental NGOs, and community groups to conduct PDNAs effectively following disasters. Perform Resource Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Species in Priority PAs Preparation of baseline of Ecosystem Goods and Services (EGS) for each target site through National Capital Accounting (NCA) Preparation of baseline on benefits (each target site) of EGS to local trade and economy, including downstream communities through resource valuation Investment planning (each target site) to generate funds and other resources to restore and protect the sources of EGS. Developing agreements (each target site) for PES to generate additional funds to conserve the sources of EGS and designing fund reflows (each target site) to conserve the sources (habitats) of EGS Establish a Comprehensive Ecosystem Valuation Framework: Develop guidelines for evaluating the economic, social, and cultural value of ecosystem services and species within protected areas. Conduct Valuations Regularly: Ensure these valuations are performed periodically to monitor changes and inform management decisions and policy development. Conduct Resource/Ecosystem Valuation of Priority Species and Ecosystem Services (Targets 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) Prioritize Key Species and Ecosystem Services: Identify which species and services are most critical for valuation efforts, focusing on those with significant impacts on human well-being. Utilize a Mix of Valuation Methods: Apply both quantitative and qualitative methods to capture the full range of ecosystem services values. Establish/Institutionalize Natural Capital Accounts (NCA) for Priority Species and Ecosystem Services Adopt the System of Environmental-Economi

title: Increase Access to Green and Blue Spaces
description: By 2040, urban green and blue spaces in all cities accessible to the public increased
actions: To achieve the target of enhancing green spaces and urban planning for human well-being and biodiversity, as outlined by Target 12 and adopted by the Philippines various actions have been identified to attain the target: Promotion of City Biodiversity Index (CBI) Adoption: Develop guidelines and provide technical assistance to cities on the adoption and implementation of the City Biodiversity Index (CBI) (Target 20). Conduct training workshops and awareness campaigns to educate local government officials and planners about the importance of biodiversity-inclusive urban planning (Target 20). Expansion of Green and Blue Spaces: Inventory of Green Spaces in Priority Cities Establishment/ Designation of green and blue spaces Identify potential sites for the establishment or expansion of green and blue spaces in urban and densely populated areas. Collaborate with local government units (LGUs), private landowners, and community stakeholders to acquire land and develop green and blue infrastructure projects that can be made accessible to local residents and visitors. Prioritize the conservation and restoration of native biodiversity in green and blue spaces to enhance ecological connectivity and integrity (Targets 2 and 3). Support for LGUs in Achieving Seal of Good Local Governance (SGLG) Indicators: Conduct of Urban Biodiversity Assessment and Profiling Urban Biodiversity Management Planning Urban Biodiversity Management Plan Implementation Provide technical assistance and capacity building to LGUs to help them comply with SGLG indicators related to urban green and blue spaces (Target 20). Develop resource materials and best practice guidelines to assist LGUs in planning, implementing, and monitoring green and blue infrastructure projects (Target 20). Development and Implementation of Policy on Blue and Green Infrastructure : Adoption and Implementation of Blue and green infrastructure/Sustainable Infrastructure Framework & Roadmap with policy instrument approved Collaboration among national government agencies (DENR, Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and other relevant agencies to develop a policy on blue and green infrastructure/sustainable infrastructure framework & roadmap. Advocate for the adoption and implementation of the policy at the national and local levels, ensuring alignment with existing urban planning and development frameworks. title: Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits from Genetic Resources
description: By 2040, there is a significant increase of the benefit shared, with providers and rights holders in accordance with applicable international ABS instruments
actions: To support the Philippine government in achieving the target of increasing the sharing of benefits from genetic resources, digital sequence information, and traditional knowledge, several actions can be taken. Development and Implementation of Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) Guidelines: Develop comprehensive ABS guidelines to regulate access to genetic resources and ensure fair and equitable benefit-sharing arrangements. Establish procedures for obtaining permits and conducting negotiations with stakeholders, including indigenous communities and local governments. Capacity Building Programs (Target 20): Conduct capacity-building programs to enhance the understanding of ABS principles and procedures among relevant stakeholders, including government officials, researchers, indigenous peoples, and local communities. Provide training on negotiation skills, conflict resolution, and legal aspects of ABS agreements. Legislative and Policy Reforms: Review and amend existing laws and policies to strengthen the legal framework for ABS, ensuring alignment with international agreements and best practices. Develop new legislation or regulations to address gaps in ABS governance and enforcement. Establishment of Multi-Lateral Systems: DENR can work with relevant government agencies, such as the Department of Agriculture (DA), to establish a multi-lateral system under the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA). Facilitate collaboration with other countries and international organizations to promote the exchange of genetic resources and ensure fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Creation of Registries and Seed Banks: Establish centralized registries or databases of native species and genetic resources to facilitate access and tracking (Targets 4 and 21). Support the establishment and maintenance of seed banks and germplasm repositories to conserve and preserve genetic diversity (Target 4). Implementation of DNA Barcoding Programs: Institutionalize DNA barcoding programs to enable the identification and authentication of genetic resources. Collaborate with research institutions and academic partners to conduct DNA barcoding studies and build capacity in this area. Establishment of Philippine Access and Benefit Sharing (PH ABS) Clearing House: Work with the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) through State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) to establish the PH ABS Clearing

title: Mainstreaming Biodiversity
description: By 2040, Biodiversity is fully mainstream and integrated in policies, programs, plans, and processes within all levels of government and across all sectors.
actions: To achieve Target 14 in the Philippines and support the indicators provided, several activities can be implemented. Here are activities aligned with each indicator: Integration of biodiversity into national and local sectoral planning Conduct capacity-building workshops and training sessions for government officials and planners to raise awareness about the importance of biodiversity mainstreaming (Target 20). Develop guidelines and tools for integrating biodiversity considerations into sectoral planning processes, including the development of biodiversity indicators and targets. Establish mechanisms for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination to ensure coherence and consistency in integrating biodiversity across different sectors. Monitor and evaluate the integration of biodiversity into sectoral plans through regular reviews and assessments. Integration of biodiversity into the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System (PEISS): Review and revise the guidelines and procedures of the PEISS to include specific requirements for assessing biodiversity impacts and mitigation measures. Provide training and capacity-building programs for environmental impact assessment practitioners on biodiversity assessment methodologies and best practices (Target 20). Strengthen monitoring and enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance with biodiversity-related requirements under the PEISS. Establish partnerships with academic institutions and research organizations to enhance the scientific basis for biodiversity assessment and monitoring within the PEISS. Integration of biodiversity into extractive industries (Target15): Develop and implement biodiversity management plans and guidelines for extractive industries, including mining, oil and gas, and quarrying. Require extractive companies to conduct biodiversity assessments as part of their environmental impact assessments and mitigation plans (Target 15). Establish biodiversity offsetting mechanisms to compensate for biodiversity loss resulting from extractive activities. Strengthen regulatory oversight and enforcement to ensure compliance with biodiversity-related regulations and standards in the extractive sector. Integration of biodiversity into infrastructure development: Incorporate biodiversity considerations into the planning, design, and construction phases of infrastructure projects through strategic environmental assessments. title: Sustainable Production and Supply Chains
description: By 2040, business and financial entities have adopted Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Framework with biodiversity elements and regularly report/disclose risks, dependencies and impacts on biodiversity By 2030, Policy instruments adopted for various agribusiness types (underscoring good practice models)
actions: To achieve the national target some actions are necessary: Amendments to Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Regulations: Introduce SEC regulations requiring publicly listed companies (PLCs) to report climate and biodiversity risks following the Task Force on Nature Disclosure (TFND) Framework. Adapt new International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) reporting standards at the sector level to enhance sustainability reporting, including biodiversity-related disclosures. Enhanced Sustainability Reporting Requirements: Strengthen SEC guidelines for sustainability reporting by PLCs to include pollution and other environmental impacts, aligning with international best practices and standards. Encourage PLCs to disclose their biodiversity-related risks, dependencies, and impacts transparently in their sustainability reports, integrating a biodiversity lens into their Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Framework. Capacity Building and Awareness Programs: Conduct capacity-building programs and workshops for PLCs to enhance their understanding of biodiversity-related risks and the importance of biodiversity conservation in business operations. Raise awareness among PLCs about the benefits of integrating biodiversity considerations into their ESG practices and reporting frameworks. P romotion of Programmatic Environmental Impact Assessment (PEIA) or Biodiversity-sensitive Environmental Assessment (BDSEA): Amend Presidential Decree 586 or the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System (PEISS) to facilitate the adoption of Programmatic EIA or BDSEA, ensuring that biodiversity considerations are systematically integrated into project planning and decision-making processes. Support for Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) Compliance: Encourage and incentivize extractive industries to comply with the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) standards, promoting transparency and accountability in revenue management and resource governance. Nature Risk Mapping and Monitoring: Produce map layers showing nature risk classification and integrate them into the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) mapping portal to facilitate the identification and monitoring of biodiversity-related risks to assets. Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration: Foster collaboration among government agencies, industry stakeholders, civil society organizations, and academia to develop and implement strategies for mainstreami

title: Eliminate Unsustainable Consumption
description: By 2040, policy instruments aimed at supporting the shift to sustainable consumption and production developed, adopted and implemented
actions: To achieve the target of enabling sustainable consumption choices to reduce waste and overconsumption, Target 16 a list of actions that can help achieve the target is provided: Implementation of the Philippine Action Plan for Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP): Develop and implement strategies outlined in the Philippine Action Plan for SCP to promote sustainable consumption choices and reduce waste generation. Coordinate with relevant national government agencies to ensure alignment and collaboration in implementing SCP strategies. Promotion of Circular Economy Practices in Local Government Units (LGUs): Provide technical assistance and capacity building to LGUs to adopt circular economy practices, particularly in solid waste management and the 3Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle). Facilitate knowledge sharing and best practice exchange among LGUs to accelerate the adoption of circular economy principles. Encouraging Adoption of Food Sustainability Programs in Businesses: Department of Trade and Industry, DENR and other relevant agencies can collaborate to develop incentives and support mechanisms for restaurants, hotels, and other establishments to adopt food sustainability programs. Provide training and resources to businesses on sustainable food sourcing, reducing food waste, and implementing eco-friendly practices. Supporting Innovation for Addressing Food Commodities Imbalances: Facilitate research and development initiatives to identify and develop innovative solutions for addressing seasonal and local overproduction and undersupply of agricultural food commodities (DA). Establish partnerships with academic institutions, research organizations, and the private sector to support the development and scaling-up of innovative solutions. Inter-Agency Coordination and Collaboration: (NEDA) Establish a multi-agency task force or working group to coordinate efforts among various national government agencies in achieving the target. Conduct regular meetings and consultations to ensure alignment of strategies and initiatives across different sectors and agencies. Strengthening Education and Information Dissemination: (DepEd, CHED) Develop educational materials and campaigns to raise awareness about sustainable consumption choices and the importance of waste reduction. Collaborate with the Department of Education and other relevant agencies to integrate environmental education into school curricula and promote sustainable practices among students and educator

title: Manage Impacts of Biotechnology
description: By 2040, biosafety measures and regulations are in place and implemented.
actions: Enactment and Implementation of Biosafety Laws and Regulations: Executive Order No. 514 (National Biosafety Framework for the Philippines) provides guidance on the development and implementation of biosafety measures. Biosafety is usually lodged in the Department of Agriculture (DA) and the Department of Science and Technology (DOST). Establishment of Biosafety Detection and Identification Measures: Joint Department Circular No. 1 Series of 2016: Guidelines on the Conduct of Field Testing of Genetically Modified Organisms in the Philippines. The agencies of importance for this are the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), in collaboration with the Department of Agriculture (DA) and the Department of Health (DOH). Conduct of Scientifically Sound Risk Assessments: Department Circular No. 2 Series of 2013: Guidelines on the Conduct of Risk Assessment and Risk Management of GM Microorganisms in the Philippines. Relevant agencies include the Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Science and Technology (DOST) and the Department of Health (DOH). Implementation of Legal and Technical Measures for Restoration and Compensation: Republic Act No. 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) Relevant provisions of RA 9147 may be utilized to address damage to biological diversity. Agencies which would collaborate on this include the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Department of Agriculture (DA) and the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG). Maintenance of the Biosafety Clearing House: The Biosafety Clearing House is maintained by the National Committee on Biosafety of the Philippines (NCBP). The agencies which are listed as the competent national authorities in the Philippines are: the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), the Department of Agriculture (DA), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Department of Health (DOH) and the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG). By involving these agencies and implementing these actions collaboratively, the Philippines can work towards achieving its target of strengthening biosafety measures and handling biotechnology effectively by 2040, in alignment with the goals set out in the Convention on Biological Diversity.

title: Eliminate Harmful Incentives
description: By 2040, subsidies with unintended environmental footprint that are harmful to biodiversity are reduced/ repurposed/redirected or eliminated.
actions: To achieve Target 18 of the KMGBF in the Philippines and support the indicators provided, several activities can be implemented. Here are activities aligned with each indicator: Number of 'repurposed' incentives replacing subsidies with environmental footprints increased: (DA, DILG, DENR, DTI) Conduct a comprehensive review of existing subsidies and incentives across sectors such as agriculture, fisheries, energy, and transportation to identify those with negative environmental impacts. Develop a prioritization framework to identify the most harmful incentives for phase-out or reform, starting with those that have the largest environmental footprint. Engage with stakeholders, including industry representatives, civil society organizations, and experts, to develop alternative incentive mechanisms that promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable resource management. Implement pilot projects to test and evaluate the effectiveness of repurposed incentives in achieving biodiversity goals while addressing socio-economic needs. Total amount of ER 1-94 proceeds used for biodiversity conservation increased: Review the allocation and utilization of Environmental Rehabilitation Fund (ERF) proceeds generated from Republic Act No. 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) and other environmental levies and fines. Develop guidelines and criteria for prioritizing biodiversity conservation projects and initiatives to be funded through ER 1-94 proceeds. Enhance coordination and collaboration among relevant government agencies, local government units, and civil society organizations to ensure transparent and accountable utilization of ER 1-94 funds. Implement monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to track the impact and effectiveness of ER 1-94 proceeds in achieving biodiversity conservation objectives. Number of Biodiversity-relevant taxes imposed (e.g., share of revenue from resource use): Review existing tax policies and identify opportunities to introduce or increase taxes on activities that have negative impacts on biodiversity, such as resource extraction, land conversion, and pollution. Conduct studies and assessments to determine the potential revenue generation from biodiversity-relevant taxes and their contribution to conservation and sustainable resource management. Engage with stakeholders, including affected industries and communities, to solicit feedback and support for the imposition of biodiversity-relevant taxes. Work with the legislatu

title: Resource Mobilization
description: By 2040, financing for biodiversity related Programs Activities Projects increased to support the annual requirement of PBSAP implementation
actions: To achieve Target 19, the Philippines will need to undertake the following actions in collaboration with relevant national government agencies: Monitoring Official Development Assistance (ODA): Monitor the increase of Official Development Assistance (ODA) for conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and ecosystems. Relevant agencies include the Department of Finance (DOF) in coordination with the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA). Assessing Public Funding Share for Biodiversity Conservation: Evaluate the share of public funding allocated to conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and ecosystems from the total national budget. Agencies responsible include the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) in collaboration with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Agriculture . Establishment of Baseline for Private Sector Funding: Establish a baseline for private sector funding dedicated to biodiversity conservation programs, projects, and activities. Agencies leading this include the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in coordination with DENR and DOF. Increasing Private Sector Funding for Biodiversity: Implement policies and incentives to increase private sector funding for biodiversity programs, projects, and activities. Agencies which can address this are the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in coordination with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in collaboration with DENR and DOF. Establishment of Natural Capital Accounts (NCA): Establish or institutionalize Natural Capital Accounts (NCA) of priority species and ecosystem services. Relevant stakeholders include the DENR, specifically the Policy and Planning Service (PPS) and the Biodiversity Management Bureau (BMB), in coordination with DOF and NEDA. Establishment of Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) Modalities: Develop and institutionalize Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) modalities. Agencies which are suitable for this are the DENR, particularly the BMB, in collaboration with the Department of Agriculture (DA) and DOF. These actions, when implemented in coordination with pertinent national government agencies, will facilitate the achievement of the Philippines' target of increased financing for biodiversity by 2040.

title: Strengthen Capacity Building and Development
description: By 2040, mechanisms for continuing capacity-building and technology transfer are in place to enable policy makers, government personnel, civil society, NGOs, men, women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and in local communities, and private agencies to help achieve PBSAP targets
actions: To achieve Target 20 several actions need to be taken involving relevant stakeholders such as the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), Department of SCience and Technology (DOST), Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) and other governmental bodies, as well as civil society organizations, NGOs, local communities, indigenous peoples and local communities (IPLCs), and private agencies. Conduct Capacity Building Activities and Develop Biodiversity Modules: DENR, CHED, and other relevant government agencies to collaborate on designing and implementing capacity-building programs and workshops focused on biodiversity conservation. Partner with NGOs, civil society organizations, and academic institutions to develop specialized biodiversity modules for various stakeholders, including policymakers, government personnel, and local communities. Reference: Collaboration agreements between DENR and academic institutions, NGOs, and civil society organizations. Establish PA Certification Course Integrated in ENRA: DENR, CHED, and other educational institutions to develop a certification course on Protected Area (PA) management integrated into Environmental and Natural Resources Administration (ENRA) curricula. Consult with experts from relevant sectors to ensure the course curriculum meets the needs of biodiversity conservation and management. Increase Capacitation on Biodiversity Management and Conservation: DENR, CHED, and educational institutions to enhance conservation-related courses and training programs to increase the number of graduates equipped with biodiversity management skills. Implement outreach programs to encourage both male and female students to pursue careers in biodiversity conservation. Engage IPLCs and local communities in capacity-building initiatives tailored to their specific needs and traditional knowledge. Increase Joint Scientific Research on Biodiversity: Facilitate partnerships between DENR, CHED, DOST, research institutions, NGOs, and private agencies to fund and conduct joint scientific research projects on biodiversity. Foster collaboration with international partners for South-South, North-South, and triangular cooperation in scientific research. Establish grant programs and funding mechanisms to support collaborative research initiatives. title: Traditional Knowledge, Awareness, Education and Research
description: By 2040, interoperability of current and future information systems on biodiversity and related subjects improved through an adequately supported and secured knowledge and information platform with the appropriate accessibility provided to decision makers, practitioners and the public.
actions: Actions which will be taken to achieve the national target: Develop capacity-building programs to enhance the skills and knowledge of DENR staff and relevant stakeholders in data management, information systems, communication, education, public awareness, and indigenous knowledge systems (Target 20). Allocate sufficient financial and human resources to support the development, maintenance, and updating of information systems, as well as the implementation of communication, education, and public awareness initiatives related to biodiversity conservation (Target 19). Strengthen partnerships and collaborations within government agencies, academic institutions, civil society organizations, indigenous peoples' groups, and international partners to leverage expertise, resources, and knowledge for improving biodiversity information accessibility and management (NGAs, Academe, CSOs, IP, development partners). Develop and strengthen policies and legislation that promote the accessibility of biodiversity information.

title: Participation of IPLCs
description: By 2040, equitable representation and meaningful participation in decision-making, and access to justice and information related to biodiversity management by all genders, youth, Indigenous Peoples, differently abled persons, Local Communities, and other multi stakeholders
actions: Actions to achieve the target are straightforward. Facilitate meaningful participation of IPLCs in biodiversity management and conservation decision-making processes at the grassroots level (within the local governance units (i.e. barangay councils and Indigenous Peoples' Organizations (IPOs)). This includes the participation of women from IPLCs in decision-making processes and initiatives (NCIP, DILG). Develop capacity-building programs and educational initiatives aimed at enhancing the knowledge, skills, and capabilities of IPLCs in biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource management, and advocacy for their rights. (Target 20)Promote community-based resource management approaches that empower IPLCs to actively engage in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of biodiversity conservation efforts in their areas (DENR, LGU). Ensure coherence and integration of biodiversity conservation policies and programs with broader national development agendas, including poverty alleviation, sustainable livelihoods, and climate change adaptation, to benefit IPLCs Facilitate access to resources, benefits, and support services for IPLCs to enhance their capacity to engage effectively in biodiversity management initiatives and derive sustainable livelihoods from natural resources. Encourage collaborative partnerships and networking among government agencies, civil society organizations, academic institutions, and IPLCs to promote inclusive and participatory approaches to biodiversity management and conservation (Target 20). Establish robust monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to track progress, assess the impact, and address challenges related to the equitable and inclusive participation of IPLCs in biodiversity management initiatives.

title: Gender Equality
description: By 2040, full, equitable, inclusive, effective, and gender-responsive representation and participation in decision- making, and access to justice and information related to biodiversity by all genders, youth, Indigenous Peoples, differently abled persons, Local Communities, and other multi stakeholders
actions: Activities currently being undertaken are in varying levels of implementation. Constant capacity building activities in the NGAs and more specially in the LGUs to mainstream gender considerations into local development plans, policies, and programs e.g., training sessions, technical assistance, and guidance on integrating gender-responsive approaches to local governance structures and decision-making processes (DILG, PCW, etc.).. Establishing robust monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to track progress towards gender equality in biodiversity conservation efforts at the local level. Collect data, conduct gender analysis, and regularly assess the impact of interventions on women, indigenous peoples, and other marginalized groups to ensure accountability and effectiveness. The list of indicators to track progress are long, it also shows that they can only be achieved by consolidating inputs from several national agencies, NGOs and POs.
